## Regex Find & Replace, multiple cursors, legacy encodings, better math, and a steadier terminal

Builds on **0.1.37**, which brought the real terminal, folder-wide search and split editor groups. This release makes the editor feel more like VS Code: regex Find & Replace, Ctrl+D multi-cursor and whole-step undo. Files in GBK, Big5, Shift JIS and Latin-1 now open and save in their own encoding. Math gets easier to write and renders Chinese text. Crash recovery covers more cases, and the terminal is tidier.

### Find & Replace
- Find has VS Code's toggles: **Match Case** (Alt+C), **Whole Word** (Alt+W) and **Regular Expression** (Alt+R). An invalid pattern turns the field red and says why; it never crashes.
- The Aa, ab and .* toggles show when they're on, with a tinted fill and an accent border, in the editor and in Find in Files.
- With a regex, Replace expands `$1`, `${name}`, `$&` and `\n`. **Replace All** (Ctrl+Alt+Enter) is one edit, and one Ctrl+Z undoes it. Enter in the Replace field replaces the current match.
- Find as you type selects the first match from the caret and scrolls it into view, even when a large file's background scan finds it later. The fields have Find / Replace placeholders.
- **Find in Files** uses the same matcher and toggles, and ignores case unless Match Case is on, just like Find in the editor. A regex can span lines, and Replace All expands `$1` and writes each file back in its own encoding.
- Find stays fast in a 100 MB file, with the current match selected and filled.

### Editing
- **Ctrl+D** works as VS Code's Add Selection to Next Find Match. The first press takes the word at the caret, matched as a whole word with its case. Each further press adds the next match, wrapping around. Typing edits every selection as one undo step, and Escape goes back to one cursor.
- **Alt+Click** adds a cursor. **Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down** (and Shift+Alt+Up/Down) add one above or below.
- Typing `(`, `[`, `{`, `"`, `'` or `` ` `` over a selection wraps it instead of replacing it, at every cursor, and one Ctrl+Z undoes each wrap.
- Typing over a selection is one undo step. Before, Ctrl+Z left the first typed character behind.
- Python: Enter between auto-closed brackets keeps the indent, and Enter after `return` or `pass` outdents.

### Encodings
- Files that aren't UTF-8 open in the encoding Malgel is confident about (GBK, GB18030, Big5, Shift JIS, Latin-1) and are saved back in it. A UTF-8 byte-order mark is kept.
- The status bar always shows the encoding. Its menu offers **Reopen with Encoding** and **Save with Encoding** (UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM, UTF-16 LE/BE, GBK, GB18030, Big5, Shift JIS, Latin-1), with the current one checked.
- Malgel won't save a character the encoding can't hold, and the message says which character it is and on which line.
- Find in Files and Replace All read GBK, Latin-1 and UTF-16 files and write them back in their own encoding. Files they can't safely rewrite are skipped and counted.
- A file with mixed line endings loads cleanly. Each `\r\n` becomes a line break, and the file is saved with one line ending throughout.

### Math in Markdown
- **Convert \[ \] / \( \) math to $$ / $** (Command Palette, Format ▸ Document, or the hint bar that appears when a note uses them) rewrites LaTeX-style delimiters into the `$$` / `$` form the preview renders. Code, `\left[` and escaped brackets are left alone. One Ctrl+Z undoes the whole conversion, and the view stays where you were reading.
- Chinese text in formulas (`\text{中文}`, full-width punctuation) renders instead of drawing boxes. Malgel uses your system's CJK fonts, and says so when there are none.
- ```` ```typst-math ```` fences are typeset as native Typst math in the preview and in HTML, PDF and Word export.
- `|x|` and `\|v\|` become proper absolute value and norm bars, including nested ones like `|a - |b||`. The `\boxed` frame is drawn in the text colour, so it shows in dark themes. `\frac{1}{T}\sum` comes out right.
- A formula that doesn't typeset shows its source in the error colour, with Typst's reason on hover. Inline math does this too.

### Large files and performance
- A 10 MB single-line file stays responsive with word wrap on. Arrow keys went from about 1.5 s to about 60 ms, and peak memory dropped from 1.2 GB to 270 MB. CI gates this.
- The large-file bar names the file's size on disk. Its message wraps instead of being cut off, and its buttons stay visible in narrow windows.
- Preview render caches (formulas, diagrams, Typst files) are size-capped. Terminal input, navigation and closed-editor histories are bounded too.

### Crash safety and recovery
- If Malgel crashes, it writes every unsaved buffer to recovery, and the next launch restores them. Background work is isolated, so one failing task can't take down the window.
- Recovered documents keep their encoding: a GBK or BOM file comes back byte for byte.
- The recovery folder is capped by age, count and size. Warnings, errors and crash reports go to a size-rotated log (5 MiB × 3) with local timestamps, the build and the commit.

### Settings, Explorer and window
- Hand edits to `settings.json` apply right away and survive in-app changes. A file that doesn't parse is reported and leaves your settings as they were.
- The Settings dialog fits small windows and is wide enough for its switches. Filtering no longer moves the card.
- A long document name in the title bar truncates instead of running under the menu and buttons.
- Explorer: a rename the filesystem refuses no longer deletes the entry, and F2 selects the name without its extension. Rename, move and create failures are explained in plain words ("you don't have permission to change this folder").

### Terminal
- Shift+PgUp/PgDn, Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down and Shift+Home/End scroll the scrollback, as in VS Code. The scrollback cap can be set (`terminal_scrollback`, default 10,000).
- Ctrl+Shift+` opens a new terminal, even from inside one. Tabs are named after what's running in them ("1: bash", "2: vim").
- Programs that ask for the mouse (tmux, vim, htop) get clicks, drags and the wheel, one report per wheel notch. On the alternate screen without mouse mode, the wheel scrolls `less` and similar programs.
- A minimum contrast ratio (VS Code's, 4.5 by default: `terminal_minimum_contrast_ratio`) keeps coloured text readable in the light theme.
- There's one caret, at the cursor, where the IME composes and its candidate window opens. The cursor shows focus and the shape the program asks for.
- When a program hides the cursor (`tput civis`, `top`), keys still go to the terminal, not the open document.
- Tabs line up at every eighth column. Selection works as in VS Code: drag, double-click for a word, triple-click for a line, Shift+click to extend.
- Typing closes the context menu, and the panel gives way when the window shrinks.
